newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's on course for 1997 profit - research unit.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's on course for 1997 profit - research unit.

text.p: Lloyds of London insurance market is on track for a profit in 1997, albeit lower than that forecast for 1996, Syndicate Underwriting Research Limited (SURL), a part of Anton Jardine Holdings Limited, said in its latest market report.
"Assuming a capacity of 10.2 billion stg in 1997, we would anticipate an average bottom line return for Lloyd's overall of only around four percent of capacity in a normal loss year," SURL said.
Lloyd's has capacity -- the maximum amount of premium income it can underwrite -- of almost 10 billion stg this year, on which SURL forecasts a six percent return.
This compares with an actual return of 17.9 percent for the 1993 year and estimates of 10.3 percent and 9.5 percent for 1994 and 1995 respectively. Lloyd's reports its results three years in arrears.

The downturn in profitability reflects the cyclical nature of the insurance industry, with years of high return usually being followed by more competitive pricing until an upturn in claims reverses the trend.
SURL's combined market report and syndicate reviews looks at all of the 170 or so active Lloyd's underwriting syndicates and rates each one, according to quality and volatility.

SURL's nine-strong team bases its qualitative assessment on a syndicate's underwriting team and strategy, management controls and the level of market support as well as the annual report and accounts.
SURL also gathers intelligence through its market contacts, managing director Mark Hewlett told Reuters.
The volatility rating takes account of risk levels, with motor syndicates being seen as low risk and excess of loss business at the high end of the risk rating.
The underwriting index is updated on a quarterly basis and includes an analysis of rating trends in key market sectors.
"We put rate movements in some sort of context and explain what they mean in terms of profitability," SURL director Dominic Simpson told Reuters.
Hewlett said the company's research differed from that of Standard and Poor's and others in that it was based equally on quantitaive and qualitative analysis.

SURL, which expects to be in profit towards the end of next year, already has several major clients, including Lloyd's member agents, and is about to sign a deal with a leading London-based finance house, he said.
SURL's target market also includes traditional Lloyd's investors, known as Names, corporate advisers, investment houses and insurance companies.

Hewlett said the company had advised on potential takeovers in the Lloyd's market, where such activity is on the increase following the recent implementation of the market's reconstruction and renewal plan.

The combined report and syndicate reviews is currently available in printed format and will also be available electronically on Reuters Insurance Briefing, the specialist insurance market service produced by international news and information organisation Reuters Holdings Plc, Hewlett said
